Subject: Post-demo hosted suitability: quickstart path + rate-limit asks

Hi Kyle / Susan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. I wanted to capture the quick follow-ups we discussed so Ledgerly can validate Hosted as the first evaluation lane. High level from our side: Hosted API looks like the simplest way to start the pilot given your timeline, but we flagged three operational items that will determine fit and next steps.

1) Traffic & endpoints: your plan is ~3k users/day, mostly text-generation with short prompts (~30–80 tokens) and the occasional long-document summarize (1–2k tokens). You mentioned 4 distinct logical endpoints (compose, classify, summarize, recommendations). Please confirm if those maps are correct.

2) Rate limits & concurrency: the hosted trial comes with per-endpoint rate caps. To avoid early throttling we need your expected concurrent requests-per-second per endpoint and 99th percentile latency targets. We can propose a temporary uplift for the pilot (short-term burst) if needed.

3) Data controls & telemetry: Hosted supports redaction, request-level logs retention options, and routing to a VPC egress for enterprise customers. For the pilot, confirm if Sandbox-level telemetry is acceptable, or if you require VPC/on-prem for compliance reasons.

Attachments: I attached a short worksheet (ledgerly-deployment-answers.pdf) you can fill in; also a one-page endpoint mapping CSV for your engineering lead. Link to our quickstart playbook included at the bottom.

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the worksheet with traffic/concurrency numbers by COB Fri (Oct 22).
- We provision a Hosted evaluation space and share staging endpoints (two endpoints initially: compose + summarize) within 48 hours of receiving the worksheet.
- If you need higher per-endpoint rate caps, we can escalate to provide a temporary increase for the pilot (subject to additional billing).

If Hosted constraints look tight after you fill the worksheet, we'll propose a Dedicated capacity check (short technical pass) or a Private deployment discussion depending on compliance. For now, Hosted is the fastest path.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to walk through the worksheet.

—
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference

Lauren — thanks for the clear summary. Susan and I went through the worksheet and added some notes inline (attached). Quick answers here:

- Endpoints: compose, classify, summarize, recs — yes, those are the four.
- Typical prompt sizes: compose ~60 tokens average; classify ~15 tokens; summarize bursts to 1.2k tokens ~5% of calls.
- Concurrency: baseline 25 concurrent reqs across endpoints during peak (US evening PST), peak burst up to 120 concurrent for ~90s during marketing pushes.
- Latency target: p95 under 450ms for compose/classify; summarize p95 under 1.2s is fine.
- Data controls: for the pilot we can accept Sandbox telemetry/retention for 30 days; production will need VPC egress and KMS.

We attached "ledgerly-deployment-answers.pdf" with a bit more detail. If you can provision staging endpoints (compose + summarize) and share credentials, we’ll run a quick smoke test next week.

Also: is token billing visible per-endpoint in the console during the trial? We want to track cost during our smoke tests.

—Kyle
Product Lead | Ledgerly
kyle@ledgerly.com

Great notes, Kyle — this is very helpful. Answers inline below and a quick proposal:

- Endpoints & staging: we will stand up two staging endpoints (compose + summarize) tomorrow morning PST. Those endpoints will be backed by the same model family we demoed.

- Rate limits: default trial caps are 50 rps per endpoint, 5 concurrent per API key for sustained calls. Given your burst profile (120 concurrent for 90s) we can:
  a) Provision a temporary burst-cap increase to 200 concurrent across the account for the pilot (48–72 hour window) — requires a short agreement addendum; or
  b) Add a small dedicated concurrency cushion by spinning up a short-lived Dedicated pool (1–2 nodes) for the first week of load testing — higher cost but predictable throughput.

- Token billing visibility: yes — Console will show token usage broken down by endpoint and model in near real-time. We'll give Ledgerly a billing view for the trial.

- Data controls: Sandbox telemetry is OK for pilot. For production we can walk through Private (VPC) onboarding and KMS integration; it typically adds ~3–6 weeks to timeline depending on legal review.

Action items:
- Kyle / Susan: confirm you want the temporary burst uplift (option a) or the short Dedicated cushion (option b) by EOD tomorrow so we can provision.
- Aditya / Rishi: please block time Thurs 9:30am PT for a brief smoke-test sync and handoff; I’ll share staging keys once we’re up.

Attachment: redwood-quickstart-endpoint-matrix.csv (simple mapping of endpoints -> sample payloads -> expected rate).

—
Lauren
